11	# Fizeau rename old-name allowlist
12	
13	This note defines the old-name taxonomy for the Fizeau rename before
14	mechanical implementation starts. It is a decision artifact only: no code,
15	configuration, or existing documentation is renamed here.
16	
17	The active target names come from `docs/research/rename-fizeau-2026-04-27.md`:
18	
19	- Project, repository, Go module, and root package: `fizeau`
20	- CLI binary: `fiz`
21	- Config and state namespace: `fizeau`
22	- Environment prefix: `FIZEAU_*`
23	
24	The rename has no compatibility window. Active runtime behavior must not keep
25	reading old paths, env vars, module paths, or command names as aliases.
26	
27	## Taxonomy
28	
29	| classification | meaning for rename beads |
30	|---|---|
31	| forbidden | Old product-name surface must not remain in active code, public docs, install/update flows, tests that assert supported behavior, release assets, or examples. Rename it to the Fizeau target or remove it. |
32	| historical | Old surface may remain only as evidence of what existed at the time: archived research, HELIX history, changelog entries, DDx tracker/audit records, execution artifacts, old release notes, and old command transcripts. Do not rewrite history just to satisfy a grep. |
33	| domain-allowed | The string may remain in active material only when it is not the product identity, or when it is explicitly negative migration/detection text saying the old surface is unsupported. These uses must not create a working compatibility alias. |
34	| external-standard | The string belongs to a separate standard or integration namespace that this rename does not own. Preserve it unless a separate governing artifact changes that external contract. |
35	
36	## Kill list and allowlist
37	
38	| old-name surface | active classification | forbidden active uses | allowed contexts |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/agent` | forbidden | `go.mod`, Go imports, README install snippets, website examples, generated docs, release/update URLs, and new instructions must use the Fizeau module/repository path. | Historical references may remain in archived research, HELIX plans, changelog entries, old release evidence, `.ddx/` audit data, and DDx execution artifacts. Domain-allowed active migration text may cite it only as the unsupported old module path, paired with the Fizeau replacement. |
41	| root `package agent` | forbidden | Root Go files must move to `package fizeau`. New root-package examples, tests, and godoc must not preserve `package agent` as the supported package name. | Historical code snippets and inventory notes may retain it. Generic prose about "an agent" is domain-allowed, but exact root-package declarations are not. |
42	| `ddx-agent` | forbidden | Supported CLI command, `cmd/` path, Makefile targets, installer/updater names, release asset names, docs examples, website copy, and active benchmark operator instructions must use `fiz` or the final Fizeau benchmark binary name. | Historical transcripts, old release evidence, archived benchmark comparisons, and cleanup/rename inventories may retain it. The DDx CLI command phrase `ddx agent` with a space is domain-allowed because it names DDx's agent subsystem, not this product binary. |
43	| `DDX Agent` / `DDx Agent` | forbidden | Active product title, README heading, website content, package comments, UI/log branding, docs that describe current behavior, and release notes for new versions must say `Fizeau`. | Historical docs may keep the old product title. Lower-case generic references such as "a DDx agent run" are domain-allowed when they refer to DDx orchestration rather than the product brand. |
44	| `.agent` | forbidden | Supported project-local config, session, cache, fixture, or example paths must move to `.fizeau` or the chosen Fizeau path. Active code must not read `.agent` as a fallback alias. | Historical examples may remain. Negative detection or warning text may mention `.agent` only to tell users it is obsolete. `.agents/` is external-standard and is not the same surface; do not mechanically rename `.agents/skills/**`. |
45	| `~/.config/agent` | forbidden | Supported XDG config paths and docs must use `~/.config/fizeau`. Active config loading must not read `~/.config/agent` as a compatibility path. | Historical docs may remain. Domain-allowed active migration or error text may mention `~/.config/agent` only as an unsupported old path and must point to `~/.config/fizeau`. |
46	| `AGENT_*` | forbidden | Exported env vars for provider config, debug flags, install options, harness record mode, tests, scripts, docs, and examples must use `FIZEAU_*` when they are owned by this repository. | Historical evidence may remain. Domain-allowed active uses are limited to local, unexported implementation variables that do not document or consume a process env contract, or negative tests/docs proving old env vars are rejected. |
47	| `DDX_AGENT_*` | forbidden | Fizeau-owned env vars for binary selection, benchmark metadata, harness quota caches, auth/session overrides, tests, scripts, and docs must not remain as supported active env names; use `FIZEAU_*` or a more specific Fizeau-owned prefix. | Historical evidence may remain. External-standard use is allowed only if a separate DDx-owned contract explicitly defines a `DDX_AGENT_*` variable outside this product's namespace; cite that contract at the use site. |
48	
49	## External standards not in the kill list
50	
51	These strings look similar to old product names but are not Fizeau product
52	identity and should not be renamed by mechanical old-name beads:
53	
54	- `AGENTS.md`: repository instruction file convention for coding agents.
55	- `.agents/skills/**`: agentskills.io-compatible local skill directory.
56	- `.claude/agents/**` or other harness-local agent directories.
57	- Generic nouns and type descriptions such as `agent`, `agent loop`,
58	  `agent run`, `agent harness`, and `agent service` when they describe the
59	  domain rather than the product brand.
60	
61	## Mechanical rename guidance
62	
63	1. First replace forbidden active surfaces in source, tests, build scripts,
64	   install/update flows, website content, README/CONTRIBUTING, and routing docs.
65	2. Exclude `.git/`, `.ddx/`, DDx execution evidence, archived research, and
66	   explicitly historical HELIX artifacts from mechanical grep gates unless a
67	   follow-up bead names one of those files.
68	3. Keep any active old-name mention narrowly worded as negative migration or
69	   rejection text. The old string should not be accepted as a working alias.
70	4. Treat `.agent` and `.agents/` as different strings. The former is old
71	   product config state; the latter is an external skill standard.
72	5. For env vars, distinguish public process env names from local shell or Go
73	   variable names. Public env names matching `AGENT_*` or `DDX_AGENT_*` are
74	   forbidden unless an explicit external DDx contract is cited.
75

85	- `ddx-agent`: classified above as forbidden for the product CLI and historical
86	  or domain-allowed for old evidence and the separate `ddx agent` command.
87	- `DDX Agent` / `DDx Agent`: classified above as forbidden for product branding
88	  and historical/domain-allowed for old docs or generic DDx orchestration prose.
89	- `.agent`: classified above as forbidden for product config state, historical
90	  for old evidence, and external-standard only for the distinct `.agents/` path.
91	- `~/.config/agent`: classified above as forbidden as a supported config path
92	  and historical/domain-allowed only for old evidence or unsupported-path hints.
93	- `AGENT_*`: classified above as forbidden for Fizeau-owned public env vars and
94	  historical/domain-allowed only for evidence, local non-env variables, or
95	  rejection tests.
96	- `DDX_AGENT_*`: classified above as forbidden for Fizeau-owned public env vars,
97	  historical for evidence, and external-standard only with an explicit separate

10	
11	This is a decision artifact only. It audits exported Go symbols containing
12	`Agent`/`agent` and decides whether each is product branding that must become
13	Fizeau, or domain terminology that should remain.
14	
15	## Audit Commands
16	
17	```bash
18	rg -n '\b(DdxAgent|AgentInfo|AgentName|[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*Agent[A-Za-z0-9]*|Agent[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)\b' *.go --glob '*.go'
19	rg -n '\b(DdxAgent|AgentInfo|AgentName|[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*Agent[A-Za-z0-9]*|Agent[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)\b' --glob '*.go' internal agentcli cmd
20	rg -n '^type |^func |^var |^const ' *.go
21	```

23	## Decision Table
24	
25	| symbol / surface | location | decision | reason |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| `DdxAgent` | root package, `service.go` | rename | Product-specific public service interface. It names this module rather than the generic LLM-agent domain. Rename to `Fizeau` or `FizeauService` in the dedicated public API rename bead. |
28	| `New(...) (DdxAgent, error)` | root package, `service.go` | update signature with interface rename | Constructor name can remain `New`, but its return type should follow the `DdxAgent` rename. |
29	| `ServiceOptions` comments mentioning `DdxAgent` | root package, `service.go` | update prose | Comments describe the public product service and should use the renamed interface. |
30	| `UsageReportOptions` comments mentioning `DdxAgent.UsageReport` | root package, `service_session_projection.go` | update prose | Comment should follow the public interface rename. |
31	| `AgentInfo` | `internal/benchmark/external/termbench/trajectory.go` | keep | Domain/schema term from Terminal-Bench/Harbor trajectory output: identifies the executor recorded in a benchmark trajectory, not product branding. |
32	| `AgentName` | not currently defined | no code action | No exported Go symbol named `AgentName` exists in the current tree. If introduced later as product branding, it should use `FizeauName`; if it identifies a benchmark executor, it may remain domain terminology. |
33	| `SurfaceAgentOpenAI` / `SurfaceAgentAnthropic` | `internal/modelcatalog` | keep | Internal model-catalog surface names distinguish agent-compatible provider APIs from other possible catalog surfaces. This is domain terminology, not product branding. |
34	| `DefaultAgentTimeoutSec` | `internal/benchmark/external/termbench` | keep | Mirrors benchmark task semantics: an agent has a wall-clock budget. Not product branding. |
35	| `MaxAgentTimeoutSec` | `internal/benchmark/external/termbench` | keep | Mirrors benchmark task semantics and YAML field naming. Not product branding. |
36	| `HarborAgent` | `cmd/bench/matrix.go` | keep | Refers to the Harbor adapter's agent class/name in benchmark metadata. Product-facing label values may change under benchmark label beads, but the field name is domain-specific. |
37	| `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError` | agentcli tests / process behavior | keep | Describes a generic child-agent process failure category, not Fizeau branding. |

1	# Project rename — Fizeau / fiz
2	
3	**Status: ADOPTED.** Use these names in code, packaging, and commits effective immediately.
4	
5	Date: 2026-04-27
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Prior renames (from git history): `luce → lucebox`. Current working name: `agent`.
10	
11	One of the project's stated goals is supporting **testing**, **optimization**, and **one-shot results** — which is also why it has no TUI. The naming exploration was scoped to metaphors that fit that one-shot framing: scientists known for a single decisive experiment, famous sharpshooters, and golfers known for hole-in-one / albatross shots.
12	
13	## Proposed names
14	
15	- **Project / repo / package**: `fizeau`
16	- **CLI binary**: `fiz`
17	
18	## Why Fizeau
19	
20	Hippolyte Fizeau (1849) measured the speed of light using a single rotating toothed wheel and a mirror 8 km away — one precise measurement, one clean answer. The metaphor maps unusually well:
21	
22	- **One shot**: one rotation of the cog → one measurement
23	- **Precision over throughput**: not Monte Carlo, not statistical sampling — a single carefully-instrumented observation
24	- **No interactivity**: the cog spins, the light returns or it doesn't. No TUI in the apparatus.
25	- **Bonus**: the Fizeau–Foucault apparatus is literally a measurement *harness*
26	
27	Predates and is more on-brand than Foucault, who is overloaded philosophically.
28	
29	## Availability snapshot (checked 2026-04-27)
30	
31	| Slot | Status |
32	|---|---|
33	| PyPI `fizeau` | Free (404) |
34	| npm `fizeau` | Free (404) |
35	| PyPI `fiz` | Taken but empty/abandoned (no description, no author) |
36	| npm `fiz` | Taken — old fis3 plugin tool, last release 1.4.5, dormant |
37	| GitHub `fizeau` repos | Top hit: `averne/Fizeau` (467★, Nintendo Switch color tool). No AI/dev/agent collisions. |
38	| GitHub `fiz` short name | Some noise: FizzBuzz, `facebook/fizz` (TLS-1.3, different spelling), `fizsh`. No agent/eval tooling. |
39	| `/usr/bin/fiz*`, `/usr/local/bin/fiz*` | Nothing installed |
40	| `fizeau.dev` / `fizeau.io` | DNS doesn't resolve (likely registrable) |
41	| `fiz.dev` | Resolves (likely parked) |
42	
43	## Other names considered
44	
45	Scientists: **eratos** (Eratosthenes — clean, good story), **eddington** (1919 eclipse, mild collision with cycling/astronomy), **cavendish** (heavy collision — Cavendish Lab, banana cultivar), **millikan** (workable, less euphonic).
46	
47	Sharpshooters: **hathcock** (Carlos Hathcock, near-zero collision, slightly grim), **hayha** (Simo Häyhä, darker connotation), **oakley** (killed by sunglasses brand), **deadeye** (generic but clean in AI/dev space).
48	
49	Golf / hole-in-one: **sarazen** (Gene Sarazen's 1935 "shot heard round the world", uncommon), **albatross** (heavy collision), **ace** (no wiggle room).
50	
51	Other one-shot motifs: **ricochet**, **potshot**, **breakshot**.
52	
53	Fizeau won on theme fit + cleanest namespace.
54	
55	## Open risks before adopting
56	
57	1. **Pronunciation split** — English speakers will hit "fih-ZOH" vs "FEE-zoh" vs "FYE-zoh". Pick one and document in README.
58	2. **Dormant `fiz` squatters** — if we ever publish a Python or Node package, distribution name will need to be `fizeau-cli` or similar even if the binary is `fiz` (ripgrep/`rg` pattern).
59	3. **`averne/Fizeau` GitHub overlap** — will share search results until this repo outranks it. Self-correcting, minor.
60	
61	## If adopted
62	
63	Follow the `luce → lucebox` playbook: repo rename, module/import paths, binary name, version bump release commit.
64	
65	## Tagline candidates
66	
67	- *"measure once, cleanly"*
68	- *"one rotation, one number"*
69	- *"the speed-of-light eval harness"*
70	
71	
72	
73	## Target Names
74	
75	| Artifact | Name |
76	|---|---|
77	| Project / repo / package | `fizeau` |
78	| CLI binary | `fiz` |
79	| Go module path | `fizeau` (e.g. `github.com/<org>/fizeau`) |
80	| Root package | `fizeau` |
81	
82	Pronunciation: **FYE-zoh** (rhymes with "size-oh"). Document in README.
83	
84	## Rename Boundary
85	
86	The rename is **broad** — every public-facing surface and internal reference is updated:
87	
88	- **Go module path** — `go.mod` module declaration, all `import` paths
89	- **Root package** — package name in `main.go` and any top-level package declarations
90	- **CLI binary** — output binary name, `cmd/` directory structure, `main` package
91	- **Config directories** — `~/.config/fizeau`, `~/.local/share/fizeau`, any XDG paths
92	- **Environment variables** — `FIZEAU_*` prefix (e.g. `FIZEAU_HOME`, `FIZEAU_LOG_LEVEL`)
93	- **Public docs** — README, godoc comments, any markdown under `docs/`
94	- **DDx dependency** — any reference to the project name in `.ddx/` configuration or execution artifacts
95	- **Release / updater** — release asset names, self-update endpoints, version tags
96	
97	## Non-Goals
98	
99	- **Historical evidence rewrites** — git history, old commit messages, and archived research docs are **not** rewritten. The rename is forward-looking only.
100	- **Backward-compat aliases** — no `agent` or `lucebox` shim commands, no legacy config migration.
101	- **Domain registration** — acquiring `fizeau.dev` or `fizeau.io` is out of scope for this rename pass.
102	- **Package registry squatting** — publishing placeholder packages on PyPI/npm to block `fiz` is deferred.
103	
104	## Config/Env Policy
105	
106	- **No compatibility window.** The rename is a hard break. Old config paths (`~/.config/agent`, `~/.config/lucebox`) and old env var prefixes (`AGENT_*`, `LUCEBOX_*`) are **not** read or migrated.
107	- Users must re-create config at `~/.config/fizeau` and set `FIZEAU_*` env vars.
108	- If a user has old config present, `fiz` prints a one-line hint pointing to the new path and exits with a non-zero code.
109	
110	## DDx Dependency
111	
112	- The `.ddx/` directory and its configuration (bead queue, execution metadata, project config) reference the project name. All such references are updated to `fizeau`/`fiz`.
113	- DDx execution artifacts (`.ddx/executions/`) are **not** rewritten — they are historical evidence. New executions after the rename will use the new names.
114	- The `ddx init` command must **not** be re-run; the workspace is already initialized.
115	
116	## Rename Mechanism Decision
117	
118	Use a committed, deterministic script for the module/import-path rewrite. Do
119	not use `gopls`/`gorename` for the module path because the change is a literal
120	repository import rewrite, not a single Go symbol rename. Do not leave the
121	mechanism to local model judgment during FZ-010.
122	
123	FZ-010 must create and commit the script at
124	`scripts/rename-fizeau-module.sh` before applying the rewrite. The required
125	dry-run command is:
126	
127	```bash
128	bash scripts/rename-fizeau-module.sh --dry-run
129	```
130	
131	The script owns only the FZ-010 surface:
132	
133	- `go.mod` module path from `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/agent` to
134	  `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau`
135	- Go import paths and active non-historical references that name the old module
136	  path
137	- `gofmt`, `go mod tidy`, `go build ./...`, and `go test ./...` verification
138	  hooks or printed follow-up commands
139	
140	Root package declarations, exported Go symbol decisions, and `cmd/` directory
141	moves remain split into their dedicated FZ beads. Those beads may use `git mv`
142	or focused manual edits where their acceptance criteria say so, but local
143	models execute the bead-prescribed mechanics rather than choosing a new policy.
144	
145	## Release/Updater Decision
146	
147	**Release repository**: The canonical release repository after the rename is
148	`DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau`. `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` is treated only as the old
149	location that GitHub may redirect from; release tooling, installer snippets, and
150	self-update code must not rely on that redirect as a supported contract.
151	
152	**Exact choreography**:
153	
154	1. Land the rename change on `master` while still in the old checkout. The
155	   change updates module/import paths, binary names, config/env names, docs,
156	   installer constants, release asset names, and updater constants to
157	   `fizeau`/`fiz`.
158	2. Rename the GitHub repository from `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` to
159	   `DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau` before publishing any renamed release tag. This
160	   ensures the tagged Go module path and release URLs are canonical at the
161	   moment downstream consumers fetch them.
162	3. Create a traceability tag named `rename/fizeau` at the rename commit.
163	4. Create the first pre-release tag and GitHub pre-release as `v1.0.0-rc.1`.
164	   The current binary version is `v0.0.8`, so `v1.0.0` is the next major
165	   without requiring a Go module `/v2` path.
166	5. Publish only new-name assets for the pre-release:
167	   `fizeau-v1.0.0-rc.1-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` containing a `fiz` binary, plus any
168	   checksums under the `fizeau` name.
169	6. Bump DDx downstream to consume
170	   `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau@v1.0.0-rc.1` and invoke `fiz`. Run the
171	   DDx integration checks there before cutting a final release.
172	7. If DDx exposes a rename defect, fix it in this repository and repeat with
173	   `v1.0.0-rc.2`, `v1.0.0-rc.3`, and so on. DDx must be bumped to the newest
174	   accepted RC before final.
175	8. Create the final `v1.0.0` tag and GitHub release from the exact commit
176	   validated by the accepted RC. Publish the same new-name asset pattern as the
177	   RC with the final version.
178	9. Update DDx from the accepted RC to `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau@v1.0.0`
179	   after the final release is live.
180	
181	**Bridge artifacts**: **No.** Do not publish `ddx-agent-*` binaries, tarballs,
182	checksums, aliases, or a final `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` release that points to
183	the renamed project. Do not add an old `ddx-agent update` bridge that downloads
184	`fiz` or rewrites user config. Existing `ddx-agent` installs stop at their last
185	old-name release and users move by installing `fiz` from the renamed repository.
186	
187	**Rationale**: This keeps the rename consistent with the no compatibility
188	window policy above: there is one supported repo, one supported binary name, one
189	config/env namespace, and one update endpoint after the break. The RC gives DDx
190	a real published artifact to validate before the final release without creating
191	a parallel old-name distribution channel that would need its own support and
192	failure handling.

10	# FZ-008 Fizeau rename branch and PR strategy
11	
12	## Decision
13	
14	Land the Fizeau rename as **sequential main commits** following the DDx bead
15	dependency graph. Do not use a long-lived integration branch and do not use a
16	stacked PR chain for the rename leaves.
17	
18	Rationale:
19	
20	- The rename has many independent leaves, but the tracker already records the
21	  safe order through explicit bead dependencies.
22	- DDx execute-bead branches carry audit commits and must not be squashed,
23	  rebased, filtered, or amended after they become part of the execution trail.
24	- A long-lived integration branch would hide breakage until the end and make
25	  conflicting mechanical rewrites harder to attribute.
26	- Stacked PRs would force frequent restacking across large string, path, and
27	  import rewrites, which conflicts with the no-rebase audit policy.
28	- Sequential main commits keep every failure attributable to one bead or one
29	  dependency cluster and give maintainers concrete rollback checkpoints.
30	
31	If repository policy requires GitHub pull requests, use one PR per bead or per
32	tightly coupled dependency cluster, always targeting `main`. Merge only after
33	that PR's predecessor beads have merged and its local/CI checks are green. Use
34	normal merge or fast-forward merge only; do not squash or rebase these PRs.
35	
36	## Merge Order
37	
38	Use this order for rename work:
39	
40	1. **Decision and guardrail setup.** Merge FZ-004, FZ-005, FZ-006, FZ-008,
41	   FZ-002, and FZ-003 before runtime rename leaves. FZ-003 installs the
42	   rename-noise checker in report-only mode, so old names are visible without
43	   blocking the intentionally mixed transition state.
44	2. **Core runtime identity.** Merge the module/import rewrite, root package
45	   rename, CLI directory rename, product identity constants, and config-path
46	   helper chain in dependency order: FZ-010, FZ-011, FZ-012*, FZ-013,
47	   FZ-020, FZ-021*, FZ-022, and FZ-030.
48	3. **Runtime external surfaces.** Merge env-var, fixtures, embedded asset,
49	   user-facing error/log, Makefile, release workflow, installer, updater,
50	   benchmark command, workflow metadata, repo metadata, telemetry, completion,
51	   model-catalog docs, and bridge-artifact beads only after their explicit
52	   predecessors are on main.
53	4. **Public documentation and downstream coordination.** Merge README,
54	   website, install docs, routing docs, demo, active-governance, migration note,
55	   external-consumer, and DDx downstream beads after the runtime surfaces they
56	   describe have landed. DDx import work must wait for the Fizeau pre-release
57	   choreography owned by the release/updater beads.
58	5. **Final stale-name enforcement.** Merge FZ-070 only after all rename leaves
59	   it depends on have landed and the report-only checker has no unallowlisted
60	   findings in the active scope. FZ-071 follows FZ-070 as the final cleanup
61	   pass for remaining allowlisted or historical stale names; it must not require
62	   weakening the active CI gate.
63	
64	## FZ-070 CI Gate Staging
65	
66	FZ-070 is not an early safety gate. It is the final enforcement gate.
67	
68	- Before runtime leaves: FZ-003 runs the checker in report-only mode. It may
69	  report old module paths, `package agent`, `ddx-agent`, `DDX Agent`,
70	  `.agent`, `AGENT_*`, and `DDX_AGENT_*` while the rename is intentionally
71	  incomplete.
72	- During sequential rename commits: local tests and existing CI protect each
73	  bead. The rename-noise checker remains non-blocking so main can pass through
74	  valid intermediate states.
75	- At FZ-070: promote the checker to failing CI only when all FZ-070 dependency
76	  leaves have merged and the allowlist represents only historical evidence or
77	  intentionally retained external-standard names.
78	- After FZ-070: any new unallowlisted old-name surface is a CI failure. Fix it
79	  with a narrow follow-up commit. FZ-071 may clean remaining allowlisted
80	  historical noise, but it should not be needed to make FZ-070 pass.

27	reasoning: low         # off | low | medium | high | xhigh | max | numeric tokens
28	tags:

30	```

33

35	# List discovered candidates
